title: LHA 120-N11 in the Large Magellanic Cloud
caption: The star-forming region LHA 120-N11 in the Large Magellanic Cloud, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope

recognition.text: Official ESA/Hubble press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Gas clouds lit in a mix of colors fill this Hubble image of LHA 120-N11, a star-forming region in the Large Magellanic Cloud. That small galaxy is a satellite of the Milky Way, circling ours in a long, slow orbit.
The Milky Way's gravity gently tugs on its neighbor's gas clouds. As they are pulled, some of them collapse and form new stars. Those young stars then light up the clouds around them in many colors.

A star-forming region is a place where clouds of gas and dust gather, collapse and give rise to new stars. In N11, the process is linked to the long gravitational relationship between the two galaxies, as the larger one's pull stirs up the gas of the smaller. The region is also cataloged as NGC 1769.

understand.summary: Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys imaged the region through blue, visual, red, hydrogen-alpha and near-infrared filters. The color mapping isn't published.
understand.eye: Long exposures, a hydrogen filter and near-infrared light reveal colors the eye could not see.
